newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZers' savings rise 8.8 pct in June yr - Westpac.
newsitem.headline: NZers' savings rise 8.8 pct in June yr - Westpac.

text.p: New Zealand household savings rose 8.8 percent in the year to June, according to the Westpac FPG Household Savings Indicators published on Thursday.

The rate was 8.7 percent in the March year. The savings rate, which excludes housing assets and mortgage liabilities, rose 2.3 percent in the June quarter against a 1.9 percent rise in the March quarter.

Westpac Financial Services chief investment officer David Beattie said the strong savings growth suggested New Zealanders were finally getting the message about the need to save, and if the trend continued it would underpin and sustain economic growth.
"This is an important and interesting result because it hints at continued economic growth," Beattie said.
"Current savings trends therefore provide some support for both the cautious stance taken by the Reserve Bank on inflation and the optimism of the Treasury regarding economic growth," he said.
The savings growth was more rapid than the rate of inflation.

The main contributors to the increase in household net worth were a 3.9 percent increase in deposits at M3 institutions and a 0.9 percent increase in other financial assets including retail pension funds and the government superannuation fund.
Beattie said Saturday's election and the Reserve Bank's suggestion that house prices had to fall five percent before monetary policy could be eased may adversely affect people's saving behaviour.
